leading_positions.synthesis: Four members prefer optical lattice clocks (Katori and Ye) as the sole prize part. They share a two-name attribution, independent reproduction of 10^-18 performance, and a view that the 2005 comb and 2012 single-quantum-system prizes are distinct from the lattice-clock concept. They differ in emphasis: Lindroth rests the case on atomic-structure physics she can judge directly, Olsson and Pearce on experimental measurement and consequences already realised, Kroll on convergence across fields. Olsson and Pearce moved to this position after reading the opening ballots, and all four attach reservations about overlap, other lattice-clock groups (Lemonde, Takamoto, Ludlow, PTB, NIST, SYRTE) and the not-yet-redefined second.

Three members prefer magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene (MacDonald, Jarillo-Herrero, Bistritzer) as the sole prize part. They share the prediction-then-observation structure, independent reproduction and the opening of a new regime of correlated matter, and all treat the unresolved pairing mechanism as follow-on physics rather than a threat to the discovery. They differ on credit: all acknowledge that Cao, Fatemi and others are outside the three-name set, Eriksson asks that the omissions be stated openly, and Mehlig opposes dropping Bistritzer. Mehlig moved here from B008 and now weighs the timing concern less than in his opening ballot.

One member prefers the Cirac-Zoller theory of quantum computation and simulation with trapped ions and ultracold atoms. The case rests on conceptual originality, decades of experimental confirmation and the cleanest two-name credit. Johansson himself concedes that B013 and B061 have broader support, and that the citation must be drawn narrowly to avoid the experimental ion and cold-atom work already recognised in 2012 and the neighbouring B050.

areas_of_agreement: The committee has two substantive clusters in the preferred configurations, B061 (four members) and B013 (three members), with a third single-member position, B034; no other ballot appears as a preferred configuration in any member's file.
Every one of the eight members names either B061 or B013 as the preferred configuration or as an alternative, and B013 and B061 are each treated by the other camp as the main fallback.
All eight preferred configurations are single-part prizes, and none proposes combining achievements.

Members across the clusters accept that the discovery claims in B061, B013 and B034 are real and reproduced by independent groups; the disagreement is about type of advance, credit and timing, not about whether the results are sound.

Several members, from both camps, say the unresolved superconducting pairing mechanism concerns follow-on physics rather than the existence of the flat-band platform, so it bears on citation wording more than on validity.
Several members note that any citation for B061 or B034 should be drawn narrowly so as not to adjudicate ion-clock priority or the experimental ion and cold-atom record.
scientific_disputes: Whether a new regime of nature (B013) should outrank a precision-measurement advance (B061); Danielsson, Eriksson and Mehlig weight breadth of new physics, while Kroll, Lindroth and Pearce weight a sharply defined, settled result.

Whether B061 is a distinct discovery or invention, or a successor refinement of the comb (2005) and trapped-ion (2012) metrology prizes; supporters read the earlier prizes as covering the comb and single-ion control, not the neutral-atom magic-wavelength lattice.

Whether a theory-only prize (B034) is a discovery in the sense the prize requires, or a blueprint whose experimental realisation has largely been recognised in 2012 and 2022; Johansson argues the proposals and the experiments are distinct, while Danielsson, Eriksson, Lindroth, Mehlig, Olsson and Pearce read the overlap as stronger for B034.
attribution_disputes: For B013, Yuan Cao and Valla Fatemi (first authors of the 2018 experiments), Dean, Young, Ashoori and the earlier theorists Lopes dos Santos, Peres and Castro Neto are outside the three credited names; members disagree on whether the omission is a defect of the list or a defensible reading of the decisive prediction and the decisive experimental programme.

For B013, Eriksson and Pearce regard a two-name MacDonald plus Jarillo-Herrero version as defensible, while Mehlig and Olsson argue that dropping Bistritzer severs the 2011 prediction he led as first author.

For B061, Lemonde, Takamoto, Ludlow, and the PTB, NIST and SYRTE groups, as well as ion-clock pioneers, have claims that a two-name credit for Katori and Ye does not capture; Kroll and Lindroth see no need for a third name, while Olsson asks whether the 10^-18 milestones belong to Ye alone or to a wider group.

For B034, the experimentalists who realised the proposals (Wineland, Blatt, Monroe and others) are largely outside the credited pair, which Eriksson and Lindroth see as honouring a blueprint without its demonstrations.
maturity_disputes: Whether B013 is ripe: the supporters point to eight years and broad reproduction, while Danielsson, Eriksson, Mehlig, Lindroth, Olsson and Pearce each name the unsettled pairing mechanism and the still-moving interpretation of correlated states as a timing risk, to differing degrees.
Whether B061 should wait for the pending redefinition of the second, or whether the demonstrated 10^-18 performance and cross-laboratory comparisons already suffice.

Whether the committee should weigh several decades of confirmation (B061, B034) against a few years of moire-platform proliferation (B013), and whether the maturity gap is a reason to prefer one or merely a difference in field age.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Kroll discloses a research stay in John Hall's laboratory and training under Sune Svanberg, a scientific lineage of the lattice-clock field but no collaboration or shared institution with Katori or Ye; he judges that no recusal is required, and Pearce and Lindroth ask that the disclosure be noted in the record.

Olsson states that she should be recused from B056 (aberration-corrected electron microscopy) because it lies in her own field and community role, and has discounted it in her preferred configuration; it appears only as an alternative.

Johansson discloses links to Chalmers colleagues Delsing and Wilson, to Kockum and to WACQT, and states he would recuse himself from discussion of B018 (circuit QED), which he has not proposed as his preferred configuration.
Pearce notes that B009 lies in his own astroparticle field; it is listed only as an alternative, and no documented tie to IceCube, the lattice-clock community or the moire community is recorded.

Eriksson notes research in electronic structure and magnetism adjacent to moire flat-band physics, and Lindroth notes field proximity to B061, B034 and B005; neither reports a collaboration or institutional tie to a credited name, and no recusal is proposed.
Danielsson and Mehlig report no specific conflict and say B013 and the other candidates lie outside or at the edge of their expertise.
questions_for_round2: Is B061 a distinct invention and measurement advance, or a continuation of the 2005 comb and 2012 single-quantum-system prizes, and can a citation worded narrowly on the neutral-atom optical lattice clock, with no claim on ion-clock priority, settle the point?

If B013 is preferred, how should the committee handle the omission of Yuan Cao and Valla Fatemi: keep MacDonald, Jarillo-Herrero and Bistritzer as listed, move to a two-name pair, or say in the citation which contributions are honoured, and what principled rule decides?

Is the unresolved mechanism of superconductivity in magic-angle graphene a maturity reason for the committee to defer B013 this year, or only a matter of citation wording around flat bands and correlated states?

Does the pending redefinition of the second weigh toward recognising B061 now or toward waiting, and do the contributions of Lemonde, Takamoto, Ludlow and the PTB, NIST and SYRTE groups change a Katori and Ye pairing?

Is B034 a discovery in the required sense, how narrowly can its citation be drawn relative to the 2012 and 2022 prizes and B050, and can Johansson say what would make it preferable to B061 or B013 on attribution and maturity?

Which criterion should decide between B061 and B013 when members weigh them differently: novelty of the regime opened, completeness and confirmation of the claim, or cleanliness of attribution, and does any member's ranking change if the criterion is made explicit?
summary.chair_observation: The eight round-1 files show a four-to-three-to-one split between B061, B013 and B034 as preferred configurations, with B013 and B061 each the stated first alternative of members in the other camp. The positions differ less on whether the results are sound than on what kind of achievement the prize should recognise and how much weight attribution and maturity should carry. No member proposes a multi-part prize, and the explicit conflict disclosures involve Kroll, Olsson, Johansson and the chair's field proximity to B009. Round 2 needs the stated criterion for choosing between B061 and B013 and an agreed treatment of the B013 credit set. This summary counts only positions explicit in the eight round-1 files.
